name: Autosomal Dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Type 2 with Giant Axons
aliases: Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Type 2 Giant Axon Variant

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for CMT2 with Giant Axons

criteria.description: Progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy predominantly affecting lower limbs
Electrophysiological evidence of axonal neuropathy with reduced nerve conduction velocities
Nerve biopsy demonstrating giant axons with neurofilament accumulation
Identification of pathogenic mutation in the DCAF8 gene or other associated loci
Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with affected first-degree relatives

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive distal neuropathy with electrophysiological evidence of axonal neuropathy and nerve biopsy showing giant axons
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical and pathological criteria are met.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Giant axons with neurofilament accumulation on nerve biopsy
searchTerms: large nerve fibers with protein buildup
abnormal nerve biopsy with giant axons

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distal muscle weakness and atrophy predominantly in lower limbs
searchTerms: weakness and wasting mainly in legs
muscle loss in feet and calves

pathognomonic.symptomName: Reduced or absent deep tendon reflexes

common.symptomName: Distal sensory loss in feet and hands
searchTerms: reduced sensation in fingers and toes

common.symptomName: Steppage gait due to foot drop
searchTerms: steppage gait due to foot drop

common.notes: Usually less severe than lower limb involvement

searchTerms: mild nerve pain in hands and feet
difficulty breathing due to muscle weakness

rare.notes: Very rare and not well characterized

laboratory: Nerve biopsy showing giant axons with neurofilament accumulation
imaging: MRI neurography may show nerve enlargement
Muscle MRI may show distal muscle atrophy
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Electrophysiological studies showing reduced compound muscle action potentials with relatively preserved conduction velocities

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of giant axons on nerve biopsy
More severe central nervous system involvement

redFlags: Rapidly progressive weakness suggesting alternative diagnosis
Respiratory insufficiency indicating respiratory muscle involvement
Cardiac conduction abnormalities requiring urgent evaluation
references: Lafreniere et al., 2019. Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 with giant axons: clinical and genetic characterization. Neurology.
